title: Inlines and Relationships
description: Edit related models on the same page using inline formsets.

slides.title: What are Inlines? 🧩
slides.content: When you have a relationship (ForeignKey, ManyToMany), you often want to edit related objects without leaving the parent’s edit page. **Inlines** let you embed a form for related models directly within the parent’s admin form.

slides.title: Example: Inline for Comments
slides.content:
Assume you have `Post` and `Comment` models where `Comment` has a ForeignKey to `Post`. To edit comments on the post page:

```python
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Post, Comment

class CommentInline(admin.TabularInline):  # or StackedInline
    model = Comment
    extra = 1  # number of empty forms to show

@admin.register(Post)
class PostAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    inlines = [CommentInline]
```

quizData.question: What is the difference between `TabularInline` and `StackedInline`?

options.text: TabularInline uses a table layout; StackedInline uses vertical layout
TabularInline is for many‑to‑many; StackedInline is for foreign keys

quizData.explanation: TabularInline displays related objects in a table row; StackedInline shows each as a separate block (more vertical space).

slides.title: Customizing Inline Fields
slides.content:
You can customize which fields appear in the inline form:

```python
class CommentInline(admin.TabularInline):
    model = Comment
    fields = ('author', 'content', 'created_at')
    readonly_fields = ('created_at',)
    extra = 0
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `show_change_link` in inlines

If you need to edit an inline object in its own separate admin page, add `show_change_link = True` to the inline class.
